title: React Backend Integration Core Check
description: Check your understanding of connecting React to APIs, REST integration, authentication flows, tokens, sessions, WebSockets, file uploads, error handling, retries, and security concerns.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Why create a central API helper in a React app?

options.text: To centralize base URLs, headers, parsing, and error handling
To make components render without state

questions.explanation: Central API helpers reduce repeated request code and keep cross-cutting behavior consistent.

questions.prompt: Which REST method is commonly used to create a resource?
questions.explanation: POST is commonly used to create resources, while GET retrieves them.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP status ranges should client code generally handle differently? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Status codes communicate different outcomes and should influence success, validation, auth, retry, and error UI.

questions.prompt: What is a session cookie often used for?

options.text: Maintaining authenticated server-side session state across requests

questions.explanation: Session cookies let the browser send an identifier to the server, which can look up session state.

questions.prompt: Storing long-lived access tokens in localStorage can increase risk if an XSS bug exists.
questions.explanation: JavaScript-readable storage can be exposed by XSS. Token storage choices should consider XSS, CSRF, expiry, and refresh flows.

questions.prompt: When are WebSockets a good fit?

options.text: Bidirectional real-time updates such as chat, presence, or live collaboration
Replacing every REST request regardless of need

questions.explanation: WebSockets maintain a persistent connection for real-time bidirectional communication.

questions.prompt: What should be used to upload a file with `fetch` or Axios in the browser?
questions.explanation: FormData is the standard browser API for multipart file uploads.

questions.prompt: What is an important security rule for React API integration?

options.text: Do not trust the client; enforce authorization and validation on the server
Send admin tokens to every browser

questions.explanation: Client-side checks improve UX but cannot enforce security. The server must validate and authorize requests.
